stories.title: AI Bubble Deflating? Dell, Workday on Deck
stories.excerpt: Friday’s tech stock bloodbath prompted much gnashing of teeth over the weekend. With stocks most exposed to AI—such as Nvidia, AMD, Broadcom, neoclouds such as CoreWeave, Nebius—falling in the 12-16% range, and Anthropic tanking on its second day of trading, it felt like the air has finally gone out of the AI bubble. Indeed, worries about AI financing are so intense that Oracle issued a statement late on Friday proclaiming that it had raised all the money it needed for its big OpenAI data center deal and any report that said otherwise was wrong—suggesting it’s a little sensitive about things.
stories.summary: The Information reports growing concerns about the financing of AI after Friday's tech stock crash, in which Nvidia, AMD, Broadcom and neoclouds CoreWeave and Nebius fell 12-16% and Anthropic crashed on its second day of trading, with Dell and Workday next.

stories.title: AI Bubble Deflating? Dell, Workday on Deck
stories.excerpt: Friday’s tech stock bloodbath prompted much gnashing of teeth over the weekend. With stocks most exposed to AI—such as Nvidia, AMD, Broadcom, neoclouds such as CoreWeave, Nebius—falling in the 12-16% range, and Anthropic tanking on its second day of trading, it felt like the air has finally gone out of the AI bubble. Indeed, worries about AI financing are so intense that Oracle issued a statement late on Friday proclaiming that it had raised all the money it needed for its big OpenAI data center deal and any report that said otherwise was wrong—suggesting it’s a little sensitive about things.

stories.title: Vulcan failure investigation focuses on ‘inadequate fuel supply’ to booster engines
stories.excerpt: United Launch Alliance said Wednesday that a preliminary review of flight data points to an inadequate supply of fuel to the Blue Origin-manufactured engines of its Vulcan rocket, rather than a problem with the engines themselves, as the reason Sunday's launch fell short of orbit with 40 Amazon Leo internet satellites aboard.

stories.title: [YT] NASA Fires Hypervelocity Projectile at Inflatable Space Station
stories.excerpt: Sierra Space recently conducted successful hypervelocity impact trials at NASA’s White Sands Test Facility in Las Cruces, New Mexico, to optimize the structural integrity of Sierra Space's Large Integrated Flexible Environment (LIFE®) habitat. The goal of this NASA-supported testing was to refine a shield for the company’s expandable, flexible space station structure to make it capable of withstanding impacts from hazards on orbit.
